pretexts: caller claims to be the company or security representative

kill_chain_signals.contact: fraudster may contact you pretending to be the company, a security representative or even someone you know
kill_chain_signals.pretext: message may claim there is a problem with your account or ask you to verify information
kill_chain_signals.movement: fraudster may be able to complete the login, change your password and take control of your account
kill_chain_signals.cashout: use the compromised account to access information; impersonate you or target people you know

red_flags: you receive a one-time passcode or password-reset notification that you did not request
someone unexpectedly asks for your password, PIN, verification code or MFA code
you receive an email or text telling you there is an urgent problem with your account and directing you to a link
you are unexpectedly locked out of an account or your password no longer works
messages, posts or transactions appear on your account that you did not make
key_quote: The code itself is legitimate but the person asking for it is not!
title: Keeping fraudsters out of your accounts
